new_scholarship.program_type: University need-based scholarship and financial aid
new_scholarship.description: Asian University for Women is an independent international women's university in Chittagong, Bangladesh, chartered by the Parliament of Bangladesh in 2006. Its Financial Aid Committee awards full and partial scholarships against demonstrated financial need, and the university states that 85% of students receive scholarship support. A full scholarship covers tuition, room and board, books, course supplies, healthcare and student activities. The university waives all fees and covers all costs for students who are first in their family to enter university and for entrants through the Pathways for Promise programme.
new_scholarship.duration: Financial aid is assessed before the start of each academic programme and continued year by year; students must maintain a CGPA of 2.5 each year to retain it.
new_scholarship.deadline: No closing date is published; applications run with the annual admissions cycle and the official pages state that admissions are open
new_scholarship.application_period: Recurs with each annual admissions cycle. As of 2026-10-04 every AUW admissions page carries the banner "ADMISSIONS ARE OPEN!" and no closing date is stated.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Women who have completed 12 years of schooling (10+2) with at least 60% in their final Grade X and Grade XII examinations, including at least 60% in English and in Maths individually, and are within 22 years of age. The university is required under its Charter to recruit primarily from South, Southeast and West Asia and the Middle East, and also accepts stateless students and applicants from outside Asia. Financial aid is decided separately by the Financial Aid Committee on assessed family circumstances, not on admission merit.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Admission is need-blind; the university states it seeks women who show high potential, leadership qualities and motivation regardless of economic background. Financial aid is then assessed by the Financial Aid Committee, which considers family composition, parental education and income, earnings of other family members, number of non-earning dependants, movable and immovable property, community assessment of the family's socio-economic status, the cost of schooling attended by the student or her siblings, the socio-economic situation of the area of residence, and luxury items owned. The Committee may investigate and verify all submitted information.

Amounts are awarded individually and are not published in a fixed table. A campus work-study programme lets eligible undergraduates earn wages on campus, and students needing travel support for summer trips home may fund them through work-study. Travel to Chittagong and the trip home after graduation may be covered only for qualifying international students on financial aid.

new_scholarship.description: The Pragati Scholarship Scheme is implemented by the All India Council for Technical Education for girl students taking admission to AICTE-approved technical institutions at degree level. Each award is a lump sum of Rs 50,000 per year of study, given for up to four years for students admitted to the first year of a degree course and up to three years for degree students admitted through lateral entry. Eligibility is limited to female students from families with an annual income below Rs 8 lakh, with up to two girls per family eligible. The scheme is applied for through the National Scholarship Portal, which lists the award as open for academic year 2026-27 with student applications closing on 31 October 2026.

Renewal requires admission to the subsequent year of the same course.

new_scholarship.description: This is the post-conflict component of the Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme under the aegis of the National Defence Fund, run by the Ministry of Home Affairs through its Welfare and Rehabilitation Board. It supports dependent wards of State or union territory police personnel martyred in terror or Naxal attacks, covering the first professional degree programme in fields such as engineering, medicine, dental, veterinary, BBA, BCA, B.Pharma, BSc nursing or agriculture, MBA and MCA. Five hundred scholarships are awarded each year in this category, split 250 for boys and 250 for girls, with quotas not interchangeable between genders. The award is Rs 3,000 per month for girls and Rs 2,500 per month for boys, paid annually after selection, and applications for the 2026-27 cycle close on 31 October 2026.
